newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian sugar cane undamaged by ex-cyclone.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian sugar cane undamaged by ex-cyclone.

text.p: Sugar cane crops were unaffected by former tropical cyclone Gillian, which crossed the Queensland coast as a tropical low with winds of about 30 kms an hour on Wednesday, the Canegrowers farmers organisation said.
The storm caused heavy rains in the Mackay cane growing region of the state, although not enough to damage local crops, now in mid season, Canegrowers chairman Harry Bonanno told Reuters.
"There was very little wind associated with the storm and it certainly did not cause any damage," Bonanno said.
The storm was continuing to weaken as it touched land south east of the port of Townsville, the Bureau of Meteorology said.
The storm failed to bring relief to the parched canefields in the Bundaberg region of the state, about 500 kms south of Mackay, Bonanno said.
"If they don't get rain, their crop could be down by 10 to 20 percent," Bonanno said.
The heaviest rains were reported in the Mackay hinterland, with falls up to 100 mm (four inches) between 9.00 a.m. and 3.00 p.m. (2300 GMT and 0500 GMT), the bureau said.
